_meta.description: Agronomic parameters for candidate crops in rotations for smallholders on the Ecuadorian coast (Guayas / Los Ríos: Babahoyo, Daule, Quevedo; 5-120 m a.s.l.). Every non-null value has an entry in that crop's 'sources' map (document name - URL).
_meta.notes: Units: cycle_days and stages_days in days; water_need_mm = seasonal crop water need (ETc) for the whole cycle, excluding conveyance and application losses and, for paddy rice, excluding puddling, percolation and standing-water losses; temps in °C; root_depth_m = FAO-56 maximum effective rooting depth Zr. kc: FAO-56 Table 12 (sub-humid climate, RHmin~45%, u2~2 m/s); Kc ini is the crop-group default (cereals 0.3, legumes 0.4) and must be adjusted for wetting frequency (FAO-56 Ch. 6). Where FAO gives a range, the value is [min,max]. stages_days: FAO-56 Table 11 row closest to humid tropics; scale to local cycle_days. temp_opt_c = ECOCROP optimal range (TOPMN-TOPMX). temp_stress_c = ECOCROP absolute maximum (TMAX), i.e. the upper limit for growth, NOT a flowering heat-sterility threshold; stress starts above temp_opt_c[1]. drought_tolerance: inverse of FAO IWM Manual 3 Table 14 'sensitivity to drought' (high or medium-high -> low; low-medium -> medium; low -> high), cross-checked with FAO-56 Ky; for crops not in Table 14, ECOCROP 'abiotic tolerance' or PROSEA. flood_tolerance rule: high if ECOCROP optimal drainage is 'poorly drained'; medium if poorly drained soils are within the ECOCROP absolute range (or PROSEA says waterlogging-tolerant); low otherwise or if ECOCROP lists flooding as a susceptibility. n_fixed_kg_ha: shoot N fixed per crop (range across regional means), not net soil N balance; grain removal exports much of it. n_shoot_accum_kg_ha = total N in cover-crop biomass, not fixed N. soil_cover from FAO Soils Bulletin 70 West-Africa USLE C factors: C>=0.4 -> low, 0.2-0.4 -> medium, <0.2 -> high; cover crops rated from USDA-ARS and IITA ground-cover observations. ECOCROP data read from the full ECOCROP DB CSV mirrored in the OpenCLIM/ecocrop repo because the FAO ECOCROP web app needs a login; values are the same database. Sources marked 'abstract via search only' were not read in full text; verify before final publication.

null_fields.rice.ky / cowpea.ky: FAO-56 Table 24 has no Ky for rice or cowpea.
null_fields.soybean.soil_cover, common_bean.soil_cov: No soybean or common bean row in FAO SB70 Table 29; no other C-factor source found.
null_fields.common_bean.season: Coastal bean trials exist in Quevedo, but no verified source gives the season.
null_fields.jack_bean / velvet_bean: water_need_mm,: Not covered in FAO-56 / FAO IWM tables; ECOCROP gives only annual rainfall, which is not a seasonal crop water need.
null_fields.jack_bean.n_fixed_kg_ha: Only total shoot N accumulation was found, not a measured fixed-N value.
null_fields.jack_bean.season, velvet_bean.season: Only experimental trials in Quevedo; no farmer season documented.

rice.grown_on_coast: Yes - major crop of Guayas and Los Ríos (Daule, Babahoyo). Main season sown Dec-Feb (rainy), minor season sown Jun-Aug (mostly irrigated). Ratoon (soca) widely used in Daule.
rice.breaks_pest_cycle: Rotating rice with an upland crop (soybean) is used in Los Ríos specifically to break pest, disease and weed cycles and exploit residual moisture.

maize.breaks_pest_cycle: Tar spot (mancha de asfalto, Phyllachora maydis) is a key foliar disease in Ecuadorian maize; crop rotation appears to reduce its severity.

soybean.grown_on_coast: Yes - Los Ríos produces ~97% of national soybean (Quevedo, Valencia, Buena Fe; Babahoyo, Montalvo, Pueblo Viejo, Ventanas). Grown in the dry season on residual moisture after rice or maize; rainy-season sowing has disease and lodging problems. Babahoyo needs supplementary irrigation.
soybean.breaks_pest_cycle: Grown in rotation specifically to break pest, disease and weed cycles; rotation is a listed preventive measure against whitefly (Bemisia spp.).

peanut.grown_on_coast: Yes, minor crop - INIAP varieties (INIAP-380, 381, 382) evaluated in Quevedo and Mocache (Los Ríos); dry-season trial Sep-Dec in Quevedo.
peanut.breaks_pest_cycle: Cercospora leaf spot and rust occur on peanut in Quevedo; rotating with grasses (maize, sorghum) reduces leaf spot, white mold and Rhizoctonia pressure.
